messages.author: 021684469a76af99
messages.subject: PDF printing fails
parts:
Hi
I have re-run analyses that already worked fine before and produced results (including PDFs with trees), but for some reason now the PDF output doesnt work anymore. I have updated all relevant libraries in R and wonder if this is the reason? 

The actual analyses are still running well (output files are all there and contain actual results); the error seems to occur after the command line:

res2 = plot_BioGeoBEARS_results(results_object, analysis_titletxt, addl_params=list("j"), plotwhat="text", label.offset=0.45, tipcex=0.7, statecex=0.7, splitcex=0.6, titlecex=0.8, plotsplits=TRUE, cornercoords_loc=scriptdir, include_null_range=TRUE, tr=tr, tipranges=tipranges)

in the section of your model script 

#######################################################
# Plot ancestral states - DEC
#######################################################
(equivalent also for all following analyses) 

the error message displayed is: 
Error in .C("node_height", as.integer(Ntip), as.integer(Nnode), as.integer(edge[,  : 
  Incorrect number of arguments (6), expecting 4 for 'node_height'

As a result the PDF contains no pages and is not being created. 

Can you help to identify what the likely problem is and how to fix it? 

Thanks
F

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] PDF printing fails
parts:
Hi -- this error happened awhile back (6 months + I think) because of a change in how the APE package plots trees.  The BioGeoBEARS code uses some of this internal APE code.  What *should* happen is that BioGeoBEARS checks your version of APE, and uses the appropriate code from before or after the APE switch.

The most obvious way this check wouldn't happen would be if you actually have not got BioGeoBEARS updated to the GitHub version 1.1, or if you have the GitHub version but also have the old CRAN version (0.21) installed in a different "lib" directory.  Sometimes it seems that you can have the new version installed, but the functions of the old version of the code.

See these tools to try and root out old versions:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/packageVersion%7Csort:date/biogeobears/2f9etrphhmg/0Jg1YIoOBwAJ

(conceivably, they might have changed APE back to the old plotting method, which worked better IMHO, but it doesn't look like APE has been updated in the last few days on CRAN; I can't speak to a GitHub version of APE)

Cheers!
Nick
